10	- **Mechanism note:** AAB-001's signed-off Zimmermann comment ("we will manage everything in the GTM container, not in Addingwell") refers to where *container/tag logic* lives — it does **not** mean Addingwell is absent from the stack. Addingwell operates as a **server-side container** routing analytics events (Third_Party_Integrations "Adding Well" row), and is the MRT integration through which the GTM snippet itself loads. Addingwell container configuration and tag routing remain out of SFCC scope (owned by Zimmermann/Tell No Lies).
11	- **Data layer** must be native to SFCC and serve as the single source of truth for all downstream analytics and marketing tags. It must cover, but is not limited to (AAB-002):
12	  - Standard ecommerce events across the full shopping journey: product viewed, product impressions, add to cart, cart viewed, checkout initiated, shipping info entered, payment info entered, order confirmed.
13	  - A complete product data schema per event: SKU, name, price, category, quantity, stock status, list position.
14	  - Local currency mapped per active regional storefront.
15	  - Customer identifiers to support cross-platform linking across analytics, CRM, and loyalty.
16	  - Attributes required for advertising platform pixel firing (Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Google Ads, Bing Ads, LinkedIn): event type, transaction data, product data, hashed customer identifiers.
17	  - Customer attributes on every relevant event: hashed email (SHA-256), login state, existing customer flag, lifetime value, customer type, loyalty status, customer group, current store view.
18	  - Customer region on every event, sourced from both Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform.
19	- Tell No Lies owns the Data Dictionary; the GTM container consumes the data layer and routes to downstream tools. 1	# 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.
6	
7	> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.
8	
9	The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.
10	
11	In scope at the PWA layer:
12	
13	- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
14	- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
15	- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
16	- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)
17	
18	Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):
19	
20	- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
21	- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
22	- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
23	- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)
24	
25	The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.
26	
27	### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies
28	
29	| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
32	| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
33	| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
34	| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
35	| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |
36	
37	In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.
38	
39	## 2. Vendor relationship
40	
41	- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
42	- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
43	- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.
44	
45	## 3. Browser-side architecture
46	
47	```
48	Page load
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
52	        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
56	        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
57	        │
58	        ▼
59	Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
60	        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
61	        │
62	        ▼
63	GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
64	(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
65	marketing consent is granted
66	        │
67	        ▼
68	Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
69	marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
70	```
71	
72	- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
73	- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
74	- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
79	- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
80	- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.
81	
82	### Loader snippets (Tell No Lies, 2026-07-01)
83	
84	Confirmed Addingwell loader snippets provided by Tell No Lies on 2026-07-01. These supersede the vanilla GTM snippet Zimmermann sent on 2026-06-10. The Addingwell loader uses a custom path (`/9i683nqysc4y77v.js`) and `awl=` query parameter (the container ID with the `GTM-` prefix stripped), not the standard GTM CDN URL.
85	
86	In `<head>` as high as possible, post-Didomi-consent:
87	```html
88	<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
89	<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
90	new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
91	j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
92	'https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl='+i.replace(/^GTM-/, '')+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f);
93	})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-M8PJ5D');</script>
94	<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
95	```
96	
97	Immediately after `<body>` (noscript fallback):
98	```html
99	<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
100	<noscript><iframe src="https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/ns.html?id=GTM-M8PJ5D"
101	height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
102	<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
103	```
104	
105	> **Note:** The noscript fallback renders when JavaScript is disabled. Because Didomi also requires JS, when this iframe fires the consent signal is irrelevant; the noscript path is a graceful degradation row.
106	
107	## 5. Data layer schema
108	
109	Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.
110	
111	> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.
112	
113	| Event | When | Key fields |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
116	| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |
117	| `view_item` | PDP load | item (id, name, brand, category, price, currency, variant, size) |
118	| `select_item` | PLP tile click | list context, item |
119	| `add_to_cart` | Add-to-bag success | item, currency, value |
120	| `remove_from_cart` | Cart remove | item, currency, value |
121	| `view_cart` | Cart page load | items[], currency, value |
122	| `begin_checkout` | Checkout entry | items[], currency, value |
123	| `add_shipping_info` | Delivery method selected | shipping_tier, items[], currency, value |
124	| `add_payment_info` | Payment method selected | payment_type, items[], currency, value |
125	| `purchase` | Order placed | transaction_id, value, currency, tax, shipping, items[], hashed email (REG-056) |
126	| `refund` | Order refunded (where surfaced in storefront) | transaction_id, value |
127	| `login` | Successful login | method |
128	| `sign_up` | Successful registration | method |
129	| `consent_decision` | Didomi banner dismissed | decision_summary (non-PII) |
130	
131	Attributes available on every event (AAB-004 Optimizely segmentation; AAB-005 Crazy Egg):
132	
133	- `storefront_region` (AU, US, UK, EU, EU-INTL, HK, ME) — sourced from Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform (AAB-002)
134	- `locale` (en-AU, fr-EU, …)
135	- `currency` (storefront base currency)
136	- `authenticated` (boolean)
137	- `customer_group` (SFCC customer group)
138	- `loyalty_status` (Retail Rewards tier)
139	- `visitor_type` (new vs returning)
140	- `existing_customer` (boolean — returning vs first-time customer, AAB-002)
141	- `lifetime_value` (customer lifetime value, AAB-002)
142	- `device_type` (mobile, tablet, desktop)
143	
144	## 6. Consent Mode v2 mapping (Didomi → gtag)
145	
146	> **Left column unconfirmed.** The Didomi purpose names below are Didomi's standard IAB TCF identifiers. Zimmermann's actual Didomi configuration may use different IDs — verify against the provisioned account once Didomi open item 1 is resolved. The right column (Consent Mode v2 signals) is from Google's official Consent Mode v2 documentation and is authoritative.
147	
148	| Didomi purpose | Consent Mode v2 signal |
149	|---|---|
150	| `measure_audience` / `analytics` | `analytics_storage` |
151	| `select_personalized_ads` / `targeted_advertising` | `ad_storage`, `ad_personalization`, `ad_user_data` |
152	| `personalize_content` | `personalization_storage` |
153	| `functional` | `functionality_storage`, `security_storage` |
154	
155	Defaults emitted before Didomi resolves are all denied (fail-closed). The update is emitted as soon as Didomi reports the user's choice. The `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call is used where regulation differs (e.g. `region: ['US']` for the US opt-out posture; rest of world is opt-in). The per-region default states themselves are owned by the Didomi configuration.
156	
157	## 7. Performance and loading strategy
158	
159	- The GTM loader script is small and loaded asynchronously, deferred until after Didomi grants the relevant consent. It does not contribute to LCP.
160	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Addingwell first-party hostname (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) is emitted from the document head once consent is granted. No preconnect to `www.googletagmanager.com` is needed — the container is not served from there.
161	
162	## 8. Multi-region behaviour
163	
164	- One GTM container ID across all storefronts (and most likely across all environments too — Tell No Lies to confirm), with region and storefront discrimination via the data layer attributes in §5. This is the assumed Tell No Lies pattern and the simplest model to maintain.
165	- Per-region Consent Mode default states (US opt-out posture vs rest-of-world opt-in posture) are emitted via the `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call. The actual per-region defaults are configured in the Didomi Console; the storefront translates Didomi state into Consent Mode signals without holding regional logic itself.
166	
167	## 9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
168	
169	| Failure | Behaviour |
170	|---|---|
171	| GTM container fails to load | Storefront unaffected. The data layer continues to populate; tags simply do not fire. |
172	| Didomi never resolves consent | GTM is never loaded; Consent Mode defaults remain denied. Pages work; analytics is absent. |
173	| A downstream tag configured by Tell No Lies errors | Tag-level — does not affect the page. GTM isolates tag failures. |
174	| A data-layer push throws | Every `dataLayer.push` is wrapped in `try / catch`; on failure the storefront logs to monitoring but never blocks the user flow. |
175	
176	## 10. Security and privacy
177	
178	- The hashed email on `purchase` is a SHA-256 hash of the normalised customer email (REG-056). No raw email appears in the data layer. Normalisation follows Google's Enhanced Conversions spec: trim whitespace, lowercase; for `@gmail.com` / `@googlemail.com` addresses additionally remove dots from the local part and strip any `+suffix`.
179	- No PII appears in any data layer event beyond the hashed email. Customer IDs are hashed when present.
180	- No card data ever reaches the data layer. PCI scope is not affected by this integration.
181	
182	## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation
183	
184	1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). **Zimmermann/Accenture** to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
185	2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) consume the data layer. The **frontend-direct** Optimizely and Crazy Egg scripts (which are *not* GTM tags — see §1) may also read it, but whether they require any PWA-emitted attributes at all is open (AAB-004 / AAB-005 — Tell No Lies to confirm; may be dropped). Tell No Lies to confirm the event and attribute schema in §5 satisfies the GTM tags, and to confirm whether any additional attributes are needed for Optimizely segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg filtering (AAB-005).

1	# 12 — Didomi (Consent Management Platform)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Didomi is the Consent Management Platform (CMP) for all seven Zimmermann storefronts. It is the gatekeeper for every third-party script that loads in the browser — marketing tags, analytics tags, heatmap and session-replay tools, the live-chat widget, the Adyen Drop-in, the Narvar EDD widget, and Google reCAPTCHA all wait on a Didomi signal before initialising.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- First-load cookie banner and consent UI
10	- Persistence of consent choices across sessions and pages
11	- Re-prompt and preference-centre access
12	- Consent callbacks consumed by application code to gate downstream scripts
13	- Google Consent Mode v2 signal emission (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`)
14	
15	Out of scope of this document:
16	
17	- The downstream tags themselves — owned by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container
18	- Server-side consent recording or back-office reporting
19	
20	## 2. Browser-side architecture
21	
22	```
23	First page load
24	        │
25	        ▼
26	@didomi/react component mounted at the top of the React tree
27	   (which injects Didomi loader from sdk.privacy-center.org)
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	Didomi SDK initialises ─────► reads persisted consent (cookie + localStorage)
31	        │
32	        ├── consent already given → fires consent.changed immediately
33	        │           │
34	        │           ▼
35	        │     App listeners load gated scripts (GTM, Inside Chat,
36	        │     Narvar EDD widget, Adyen, reCAPTCHA, etc.)
37	        │
38	        └── no prior consent → Didomi renders the banner
39	                    │
40	                    ▼
41	                User makes a choice
42	                    │
43	                    ▼
44	                consent.changed event fires with the new purpose and vendor IDs
45	```
46	
47	- The PWA uses the **`@didomi/react`** package to mount the SDK as early as possible at the top of the React tree. This is the Didomi-recommended approach for SPAs and keeps configuration tied to a single component rather than a raw script tag.
48	- The SDK's loader is fetched asynchronously from `sdk.privacy-center.org`. Configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is pulled from the Didomi Console at runtime — the loader URL itself is environment-agnostic; the per-environment Notice ID identifies the configuration.
49	- The PWA registers listeners for `consent.changed` and per-vendor status changes. Each gated integration subscribes to the specific purpose or vendor ID it requires; on grant, it dynamically imports or injects its script tag.
50	- SSR HTML must not contain markup whose presence or content depends on consent state — consent-driven UI is hydrated on the client. This keeps the SSR cache consent-agnostic and avoids cumulative layout shift.
51	- No consent rules are hard-coded in the storefront. All configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is owned by the Privacy team in the Didomi Console.
52	
53	## 3. Credentials
54	
55	- **Public credential:** the Didomi Notice ID, embedded in the `@didomi/react` component props. Safe to ship in the browser bundle.
56	- **No machine credential is required from the storefront** — the SDK authenticates using the Notice ID alone.
57	- **Per-environment Notice IDs:** separate Didomi Notices are provisioned per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) so non-production traffic never affects production consent reporting. The PWA reads the active Notice ID from an environment variable resolved at build / runtime.
58	
59	## 4. Data exchanged
60	
61	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| Browser → Didomi | None at runtime — consent UI is rendered by the SDK from the Console configuration | n/a |
64	| Didomi → Browser | Consent state: per-purpose booleans, per-vendor booleans, IAB TCF string, regulation applied, opaque user ID | `consent.changed` event and `Didomi.getCurrentUserStatus()` |
65	| Browser → GTM dataLayer | Default and updated Consent Mode v2 signals | `gtag('consent', 'default' \| 'update', …)` |
66	
67	The storefront does not pass PII to Didomi. The Didomi user ID is an opaque consent identifier — it is not joined to the SFCC customer profile and is never written to the customer record.
68	
69	## 5. Consent and gating contract
70	
71	Every PWA-direct integration that loads a third-party script subscribes to one of the buckets below. The storefront's configurable consent categories are **Performance, Analytics, and Marketing**, with **Required** always granted (REG-051). The exact Didomi purpose IDs used in production are owned by the Privacy team in the Console; the table is the application-side mapping.
72	
73	| Bucket | Purpose family | Scripts gated |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Required (strictly necessary) | Always granted, no banner consent | Didomi itself; SFCC SCAPI; Contentful Delivery API; PWA→MRT proxy reads; Adyen Drop-in — **not Didomi consent-gated**: payment is strictly necessary and the Drop-in loads at the payment step regardless of consent state. The fail-closed rule (§8) applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not payment. |
76	| Analytics / measurement | `analytics`, `measure_content_performance` | GTM analytics tags (GA4 and anything Tell No Lies routes to it); Crazy Egg (all storefronts — AAB-005) and Optimizely Web (US storefront only — AAB-004) — both frontend-direct scripts, not in GTM. **Consent categories are TBC — Zimmermann to confirm** |
77	| Marketing / advertising | `create_ads_profile`, `select_personalized_ads`, `targeted_advertising` | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
78	| Performance | `improve_products`, `personalize_content` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD **(TBC)**, Google Maps address autocomplete, Inside Chat **(TBC — consent category to be confirmed with Tell No Lies)**, Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
79	| reCAPTCHA | **EU & UK: consent-gated (TBC)** — loads only post-consent in those regions; no consent required on other storefronts at form interaction | Google reCAPTCHA site-key load on the relevant forms |
80	
81	Adyen is a payment necessity and defers load until the customer reaches checkout, so it does not contribute to LCP on any other page. reCAPTCHA likewise defers until register / login form interaction — it loads with no consent requirement in most regions, and is consent-gated in EU & UK (TBC), providing no bot protection where consent is ignored/declined.
82	
83	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
84	
85	- The Didomi loader is fetched asynchronously and is small (Didomi-reported figures put it in the low single-digit KB range gzipped).
86	- Per HPC-013/014 the Didomi notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes. The underlying LCP candidate (the hero image) still renders behind the scrim, so LCP is measured normally; the page is simply non-interactive until the shopper completes the flow. The grey-out is a confirmed requirement (subject to final designs) — the notice is not deferred away.
87	- All downstream gated scripts are deferred behind their consent callback and dynamically imported / injected. None contribute to the LCP measurement on any page — **with one deliberate, scoped exception: Optimizely Web**. On the US storefront only (per AAB-004), Optimizely is head-loaded before render so its anti-flicker snippet can suppress content flash; this exception is allowed to take priority over the LCP budget. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out and must not block LCP.
88	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `sdk.privacy-center.org` is emitted in the document head so the SDK fetch does not pay a cold DNS / TLS cost.
89	
90	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
91	
92	- A single Didomi Notice serves all eight storefronts; per-region purpose configuration is managed inside the Didomi Console. The Notice ID does not vary by region — Didomi auto-detects the applicable regulation from the visitor's IP.
93	- Per-region default consent state follows REG-054: EU storefronts opted-out; US domestic requires an explicit choice (no action = opted-out); AU, US international, HK, and ME are opted-in by default. These defaults are configured in the Didomi Console and honoured by the SDK when it loads. The fail-closed rule in §8 applies only when consent state cannot be determined (SDK load failure) and is independent of these per-region defaults.
94	- The marketing opt-in checkbox at registration and newsletter sign-up is **a separate UI control from the Didomi banner** and follows the regional defaults in the Functional Requirements (REG-057): pre-checked on US domestic only, unchecked everywhere else.
95	- The banner language follows the active storefront locale: English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, and EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic. A storefront locale switch triggers `Didomi.setUserLanguage()` so the preference centre also renders in the new language.
96	- **Open (TBD):** consent behaviour on the Global-e-owned checkout iframe origin is not yet settled — how (or whether) Didomi consent state propagates to that cross-origin context remains to be confirmed.
97	
98	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
99	
100	| Failure | Behaviour |
101	|---|---|
102	| Didomi loader fails to fetch (CDN outage, network block, blocker extension) | **Fail closed.** The Didomi Web SDK does not itself default to denied if it fails to load — the storefront implements a 5-second timeout (a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value). On timeout, the storefront acts as if no consent has been granted: GCM signals stay denied, no gated scripts load. The storefront remains functional for browsing and for SFCC checkout. |
103	| Didomi loader loads but `consent.changed` never fires (SDK initialisation bug, blocked storage) | Same as above — fail closed after the 5-second timeout; the error is logged to monitoring. |
104	| Consent is granted but a downstream script fails to load | The page does not block. The failure is logged. The customer experience continues. |
105	| User revokes consent mid-session | Previously-loaded gated scripts are signalled to disable where the vendor supports it (e.g. GTM `gtag('consent', 'update', …)`). 56	
57	The ordering above is **for reading**, not for runtime. 60	
61	- **Fail closed on consent.** If Didomi cannot determine consent state, no third-party tracking or marketing script loads.

128	- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
129	- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Local values live in `.env.shared` (tier-independent) and `.env.<tier>` (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) — gitignored, managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; full command reference in `.env.sample`'s header) — and are set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env.sample` tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on its own comment line above the key (value only if it's a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave blank — never a trailing comment, or a blank placeholder reads as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard), (2) run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold the new key into `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>`, then fill in the real value locally. Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.
130	- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
131	- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
132	- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
133	- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
134	- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. Wait for the user to confirm the overrides are rendering before making any functional changes; remove the `console.log` statements once confirmed. Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes.
135	
136	## Consent & Marketing
137	
138	- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
